And in this same year, al-Adil again took Saruj, the city of Resh'aina, and Jumlin from his nephew al-Afdal.
And also his brother Zahir, the lord of Aleppo, took the fortress of Najm from al-Afdal.
And only Samosata remained to him.
And when he saw that his uncle and his brother had wronged him,
he sent an envoy to Rukn al-Din Suleiman, the son of King Qilij Arslan, the lord of the city of Melitene and Iconium,
and entered under his vassalage, and proclaimed him,
and struck coins in his name,
and became like one of the emirs of the Romans [Rum].
For al-Afdal had sent his mother to King al-Adil,
and she entreated him to restore the places that he had taken from her son,
but he did not accept persuasion from her.
And thus God repaid King Saladin after his death,
just as he had done with the house of the Atabeg,
when the lord of Mosul sent his own mother and his cousin to him,
and he did not accept persuasion from them.
And in this year, King al-Adil expelled al-Malik al-Mansur, the son of King al-Aziz, from Egypt,
and settled him in the city of Edessa, along with his mother, his brothers, and his sisters;
for he feared lest the Egyptians should make him king.
The beginning of the kingdom of the Mongols (Moghuls), that is: Now the original country of the Tatars,
before they spread out to these outer lands,
was a certain valley, that is, a great plain in the northeast of the inhabited world,
about eight months' journey in length and breadth.
On the eastern side,
to the land of the Cathayans, that is, the Chinese,
Cathay is adjacent to their land.
And on the west,
to the land of the Uyghur Turks.
And on the north,
to the land that is called Salafghai (Siberia?).
And on the south,
to India.

and they used to pay tribute to the king of the Cathayans, that is, the Chinese.
